name: Common cutworm
signs: Young corn cut off at ground level, leaving gaps in the rows
Leaf surfaces scratched, holes, or leaves eaten down to the midrib
Egg clusters covered with a hairy scale on the leaves; worst in weedy fields
actions: Clear and till the weeds well before planting, so the young caterpillars have nothing to eat
In the morning, dig around a cut plant, find the caterpillar in the soil, and destroy it
Rotate crops and choose a clean field
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays, so the wasps and birds that feed on the caterpillars help you
callExpertIf: Many seedlings are being cut or the gaps in the rows keep growing
